Wedding bells are ringing for Miley Cyrus and her fiancé, Maxx Morando.

The rockers are planning to say “I do” in a ceremony in Southern California this weekend, according to a TMZ source.

The news of their engagement was first confirmed in September 2025, after Cyrus was seen wearing a sparkling engagement ring as they posed together on the red carpet at the premiere of “Avatar: Fire and Ash.”.

Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, have been linked since the summer of 2021. In a British Vogue cover interview, the “Flowers” singer recalled their introduction, explaining, “We got put on a blind date.”.

Sources indicate that she then provided a key clarifying detail, noting, “Well, it was blind for me and not really for him. I thought, ‘The worst that can happen is I leave.’”.

It’s safe to say the date was a success, with their love story blossoming over the last four years.

Almost immediately, they began collaborating together professionally, with Cyrus telling Vogue Morando was one of her “favorite emerging artists,” having designed sustainable looks for her to wear during her various appearances in music festivals in 2021.

Later that year, Morando’s band, Liily, performed as part of “Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party,” where the “Hannah Montana” star rang in the New Year with an NBC special.

He’s even collaborated on some of Cyrus’s most recent music, and in a Harper’s Bazaar interview, she explained the significance of bringing a romantic partner into her professional sphere.

“I worked with my dad forever. That’s how me and my ex-husband met each other,” she said. “I’ve always worked with the people that I love. And Maxx just inspires me so much.”.

While Morando appears to be quite private in regards to his personal life, he has publicly supported his soon-to-be wife at a handful of public events, including movie premieres and award shows.

According to recent reports, A few years into their relationship, the nearlyweds took a major leap. A People magazine source confirmed they had moved in together in February 2024.

“She is very happy with him,” the source revealed. “Miley has changed a lot in the past couple of years. She seems more calm and harmonious. Everyone loves Maxx. He’s a great guy. She is very happy with him. He’s private and doesn’t like being in the press. It’s been good for her.”.

Cyrus shared what it’s like to live with her fiance in a September 2026 chat on the Zane Lowe Show, where she gushed that even life’s most mundane tasks are more fun with Morando around.

I think that’s the thing that maybe generations prior didn’t teach us, that marriage doesn’t need to be a prison. It can actually be a playground,” she mentioned. “It’s just living with a best friend. And that’s what it is.”.

In 2024, an Us magazine source confirmed that although “Miley owns a number of properties,” the lovebirds are “staying at her home in Malibu,” which was described as a “huge mansion overlooking the water in a gated community.”.

Industry observers note that although Cyrus also has homes in Studio City, Hidden Hills, and her home state of Tennessee, the couple reportedly adores the Malibu home’s proximity to the sea. Apparently, they “spend a lot of time on the private beach together.”.

Cyrus has a long history of living in Malibu—and even has a song named after the coastal locale.

Industry observers note that back in 2016, she paid $2.5 million for a gorgeous midcentury modern home in the area. At the time, she shared the 1,385-square-foot dwelling with her now-ex-husband, Liam Hemsworth. The former couple used it as a creative studio and guest house.

The funky home was perched on a two-acre property with lots of lush greenery, which could be peacefully enjoyed from the terrace of the primary bedroom, according to Architectural Digest.

The singer and “The Hunger Games” star would call another Malibu mansion their home, however—a $6.8 million property Hemsworth had purchased in 2014, which was tragically destroyed by the 2018 Wolsey Fire just weeks before their wedding.

According to recent reports, the sprawling property was more than just a home. It also housed Rainbowland, her personal recording studio.

Miley reflected on the tragedy in 2025, telling People, “When my house burned down, that was the biggest blessing I’ve ever had in my life, actually.”.

She explained that after “losing everything,” having the opportunity “to rebuild” inspired her to be more “purposeful” when carefully selecting new belongings.

Cyrus and Hemsworth separated in August 2019, and their divorce was finalized in January 2020.

In the months following the split, Cyrus offloaded the guesthouse at a loss in an off-market transaction for $1.7 million, and Hemsworth sold the wildfire-damaged property for $3.6 million.

According to recent reports, it wouldn’t be too long before the “Black Mirror” actress would find herself back in Malibu. She snapped up a $7.9 million Mediterranean mansion in the city in 2022, which is reportedly where she and Morando live now.

The 1999-built property is on a 1.48-acre-lot in a gated community, which affords lots of privacy.

It’s truly a resort-like retreat, with a pool and spa in the backyard surrounded by soaring palm trees.

Indoors, an open-initiative layout boasts tall ceilings and glass sliding doors that connect the serene space to the equally-tranquil landscape.

The massive primary suite provides striking panoramic views of the beach, and has a lounge space, a fireplace, and a balcony.

Hitachi Vantara bets smarter storage can close AI’s pilot-to-production gap

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that enterprises pushing AI from pilot to production are learning that data, not GPUs, is the hardest part, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg are part of the answer.
  • Sources indicate that that pressure is turning storage into an active layer that classifies, governs and serves data to models.
  • “Storage is not seen as just storing the data,” Raman stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 13:39 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Industry observers note that enterprises pushing AI from pilot to production are learning that data, not GPUs, is the hardest part, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg are part of the answer. Demand for AI infrastructure indicates few signs of slowing, but much of the information companies need is still scattered, ungoverned and out of reach.

Sources indicate that that pressure is turning storage into an active layer that classifies, governs and serves data to models. Unstructured files such as logs and medical images hold intelligence AI can now extract, according to Arun Prasad Raman (pictured, left), vice president of hybrid cloud and AI infrastructure at Hitachi Vantara Corp.

“Storage is not seen as just storing the data,” Raman stated. “You need to bring in more intelligence natively rather than moving the data to another replication and bringing it back for, say, indexing. If it can do it natively, that’s where the value add is.”.

Sources indicate that raman and Jeff Lundberg (right), principal product and solutions manager at Hitachi Vantara, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI’s pilot-to-production gap, Apache Iceberg and how Hitachi Vantara is adding intelligence to storage. (* Disclosure below.).

In a recent development, reference architectures for AI factories and data platforms are largely settled. Most projects stall because data is spread across on-premises systems, software-as-a-service applications and the cloud, while access control, governance and shifting regulations add friction, according to Lundberg. Hitachi Vantara is responding with industry-specific solutions built on its Hitachi iQ stack and its sister businesses’ rail and energy experience, he explained.

“It’s about the outcome more so than the technology that we’re trying to put into place,” Lundberg stated. “That’s an enabler to get you to the solution you’re trying to get to.”.

Much of that work now happens in storage. Last week, Hitachi Vantara expanded its VSP One platform with new object storage and data lakehouse capabilities. A service in its object store flags files containing personal information, such as Social Security numbers. Data scientists can then keep that data out of specific models or block its replication to another country, Raman explained.

Sources indicate that “That’s the intelligence we are adding into the storage itself,” Raman stated. “So that’s where the evolution of storage is making it more intelligent.”.

Analytics follow the same logic. CT scan metadata can be stored in Apache Iceberg format on the company’s object store and queried directly. An application could list every abdominal scan from the past year without a separate extract, transform and load or ETL process or database, Raman noted.

“Whether it’s a backup or it’s 10 years old, it still carries some intelligence,” Raman said. “As long as it carries intelligence, it becomes important to AI.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as artificial intelligence workloads shift to inference, memory bandwidth decides whether hardware generates tokens quickly or sits idle.
  • AI infrastructure has become a systems game, and winners combine memory, interconnect and software into cohesive designs, according to Satyam Srivastava (pictured), fellow at d-Matrix.
  • Memory bandwidth is a fundamental advantage that has to be solved,” Srivastava noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 14:21 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

In a recent development, as artificial intelligence workloads shift to inference, memory bandwidth decides whether hardware generates tokens quickly or sits idle. D-Matrix Corp. is answering with Raptor, a second-generation chip stacking 3D DRAM beneath its compute logic.

AI infrastructure has become a systems game, and winners combine memory, interconnect and software into cohesive designs, according to Satyam Srivastava (pictured), fellow at d-Matrix.

“It’s no longer a chip problem. Chip plays a part of it. Memory bandwidth is a fundamental advantage that has to be solved,” Srivastava noted. “The next is energy efficiency. The next is interconnect efficiency. The next is software cohesiveness.”.

It has been revealed that srivastava spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed d-Matrix’s Raptor chip and its stacked 3D DRAM, inference memory bandwidth and the shift toward heterogeneous computing. (* Disclosure below.).

D-Matrix proves each risky technology on a test chip first. Jayhawk proved die-to-die connectivity, and Jayhawk II validated digital in-memory computing. The Corsair accelerator combined both and entered full production earlier this year, Srivastava explained.

“Fast forward, we have the Pavehawk chip, test chip, which is proving out 3D DRAM stacked underneath the logic die, which serves as the core technology for Raptor, which is our second-generation chip coming out next year,” Srivastava said.

Sources indicate that stacking keeps the distributed memory architecture intact but moves memory cells onto a separate layer rather than consuming logic die area. Data travels a short distance and never crosses an interposer. That puts 3D DRAM in a fresh tier between SRAM and high-bandwidth memory, Srivastava noted.

“So you’re getting 10 times higher energy efficiency compared to HBM, 10 times higher bandwidth compared to HBM, where it sits in between SRAM and HBM in terms of capacity,” Srivastava noted.

Pairing a Corsair-based server with an existing Hopper GPU fleet can raise utilization from about 20% to as much as 80%, meaning more tokens per dollar, Srivastava noted. D-Matrix has also adopted NVLink Fusion rackscale infrastructure from Nvidia Corp. to connect its accelerators to Nvidia’s AI factories.

In a recent development, “For us, it unlocks the opportunity to participate in a very established ecosystem, the world’s most popular AI factory. We get access to a very hardened design of an MGX rack,” Srivastava said.

The partnership points toward heterogeneous computing, where software orchestrates GPUs, CPUs and accelerators such as Raptor as one system, with the cluster as the unit of computing, Srivastava explained.

According to recent reports, “So think of a chip, but that chip is an entire cluster and it has many different hardware units,” Srivastava remarked. “Some are GPUs, some are CPUs, some are ASIC accelerators, and you can use whichever one you like to serve the needs of the workload the best.”.

Tech Report: The Rise of the House Manager: Why Busy Families Are Outsourcing Everyday Tasks

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Between managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day.
  • For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.
  • For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Between managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day.

For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.

For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.

Recent findings suggest that "A house manager takes on the parts of the household a family chooses to hand off—that means both the everyday work and the planning behind it, from start to finish," states Kelly Hubbell, founder and CEO of Sage Haus, a thriving house manager placement company. "Think meals, laundry, errands, calendars, pet care, and home projects. A house manager doesn't just complete tasks ... they anticipate what's needed and handle it without being asked.".

In other words, a house manager is an added support system that helps keep a household functioning efficiently.

The simplest definition of a house manger is someone who helps facilitate everyday life behind the scenes.

"A housekeeper cleans, a nanny cares for the kids, a house manager owns whole areas of the household, from planning to follow-through," states Hubbell.

Sources indicate that there can be overlap. A house manager might tidy, do laundry, or prepare meals, depending on what the family hands off. The difference is ownership.

"Take laundry: A housekeeper might wash what's in the basket, whereas a house manager who owns laundry knows the soccer uniform has to be clean by Saturday, without a reminder," explains Hubbell. "The work that's different is the thinking behind the household.".

The best house managers have sharp judgment and the ability to blueprint ahead, juggle several schedules and tasks at once, manage vendors, and make good decisions within the scope a family has agreed to, according to Hubbell.

Recent findings suggest that they're proactive and notice what needs attention before anyone asks. And because they're in someone's home, trust, reliability, and discretion are essential.

"People come to it from lots of backgrounds: nannies whose kids aged out of needing a nanny, teachers, hospitality and operations managers, military spouses who have set up a household in four cities, and moms coming back into the workforce after years of running their own homes—frankly, the hardest training there is," says Hubbell, whose network now includes over 7,000 house managers in the U.S. and Canada, though Sage Haus accepts only about 5% of applicants to ensure quality.

"As AI changes the jobs available, this work depends on what technology can't supply: human judgment, trust, and care," she explains.

Basically, house managers are gaining traction because people are burning out, especially women.

"Most families hit a point where their life, career, or ambitions can't grow any further without more support—I call that the support ceiling," says Hubbell. "They don't need to scale back their dreams. They need to scale up their support.".

Many families already have some help, like a cleaner every other week, a nanny/sitter, or groceries on autopilot. But someone still has to hold it all together—the noticing, planning, and following up.

"That's the mental load, and research indicates it usually stays with mom, even as her career and earnings grow," says Hubbell.

According to a 2024 study from the University of Bath and the University of Melbourne, mothers in the U.S. carry 71% of mental-load tasks, and while women’s employment and earnings reduce their physical household labor, it does not shrink their cognitive burden.

In a recent development, "Real estate has always recognized the value of a well-maintained home. What we're only beginning to recognize is the value of the work required to maintain it," claims Laura Marie Rivera, a gender equity and unpaid labor researcher and host of the "Motherhood Advantage" podcast. "The rise of professional house managers puts a job title and salary on responsibilities that mothers have managed for generations—largely without either.".

Recent findings suggest that unpaid household work in the U.S. is worth up to $6 trillion a year, and none of it indicates up in the GDP. However, the rise of house mangers is finally putting a dollar amount on the mental load of keeping a home operational.

"Paying someone to manage a household doesn't just reveal the economic value of the work, it reveals the scope of the work," says Rivera. "We're not witnessing the invention of a fresh profession so much as the professional recognition of work that has been hiding in plain sight.".

In a recent development, the good news is that having a house manager isn't only for the wealthy. In general, cost depends on where you live and what you need the house manager to take on.

According to recent reports, "Families hire and pay house managers directly, and pay ranges from $25 to more than $50 an hour depending on location and scope," says Hubbell. "It doesn't have to be full time: 80% of families start with part-time help, averaging 15 to 20 hours per week.".

For many families, a house manager can be a more practical investment than several separate kinds of help, because it brings that support together in one role. However, there are still options when budgetary constraints prohibit the employment of a house manager.

"Support doesn't have to start with a hire," says Hubbell. "It can begin with mapping out everything it takes to run your home and deciding what to drop, what to share with a partner, and where you need help most.".

That being noted, for those who can swing it, having a house manager can be life-changing.

It has been revealed that in theory this all sounds amazing, but what's it like in practice? We checked in with a house manager and a family that's hired a house manager to get the inside scoop. But the short version is, both are very happy with their decision.

Before becoming a house manager, Terry Boch worked as an executive assistant, but also spent years as a stay-at-home mom raising her three children.

Sources indicate that once they were grown and she reentered the work force, she was enjoying being an executive assistant again but realized she wanted something less computer-focused and more hands-on. That's when she came across a job post seeking house managers. Intrigued, she pursued the opportunity, was matched with a family in Fresh Jersey, and found it was a perfect fit for her skill set.

Sources indicate that "I love transforming an already beautiful house into a warm, welcoming home that looks and smells inviting every day," notes Boch, whose primary responsibilities include meal planning, grocery shopping and meal preparation, laundry, resetting bedrooms and living spaces, and plant care. "I work approximately 15–20 hours per week, but I like to say that I get to play house in a home I could never afford.".

In reality, however, Boch states she sees what she does as much more about creating a home than maintaining a house.

"Although my interaction with the children is limited, knowing that I can contribute to an environment where they feel comfortable, cared for, and happy brings me tremendous joy," notes Boch. "I love making a home feel welcoming, anticipating what a family needs, and taking pride in all the little things that make everyday life more enjoyable. I'm not a house cleaner; I'm a homemaker at heart.".

On the flip side, Krissel Varela found her way to the idea of hiring a house manager online.

It has been revealed that "Following Sage Haus on social media really opened my eyes to what household support could look like," says Varela. "I had always thought about help in a more traditional sense, like a nanny or someone full-time, but started realizing we could shape the support around what our family actually needed.".

Though she'd had a nanny when her kids were younger and she was working a corporate job, once they reached school age, they didn't need that kind of assistance anymore. However, their lives didn't get less busy.

"Between school, sports, activities, keeping our household running, and now building a business of my own, there are just so many moving pieces," indicates Varela. The idea of a house manager made sense for her family, though they didn't need someone full time.

Recent findings suggest that "Right now, we have help about 8 to 10 hours a week, and even though that's not a huge number of hours, the impact feels so much bigger," notes Varela. Her house manager is usually with them on Mondays and Thursdays, with some flexibility predicated on their needs.

"Between laundry, household organization, errands, and all those little tasks that add up throughout the week, having someone share those responsibilities makes such a difference," she adds.

Though it's been only a few months, Varela claims she can already feel a huge life shift.

In a recent development, "It's not just the actual hours saved; it's also the mental space that comes from knowing someone else is helping keep things moving without having to manage every little detail," says Varela. "It's also given me more room for the things that are easy to push aside when life gets busy, whether that's spending quality time with my husband, enjoying our weekends, or even having a little time for myself. Having that extra support has really helped me be more intentional about where my time and energy go.".

And that is exactly what a house manager is supposed to do, open up space for life at home to be about more than just getting by every day.

"People should also know there's a cost to getting support and a cost to going without it, whether that's your health, your relationships, or your connection with your family," says Hubbell. "The goal isn't to outsource your life; it's to get enough support to be present for it.".

Industry observers note that kimberly Dawn Neumann is a journalist based in Upcoming York City and the author of hundreds of articles on home-related topics for major publications, including Forbes, Real Simple, and Realtor.com. For more information, visit www.KDNeumann.com or IG @dancerscribe.

Latest Update: Latest York’s Luxury Rental Market Sees Influx of Cash from AI Boom

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The artificial intelligence boom has expanded from the rolling hills of San Francisco and Silicon Valley to the busy streets of New York City, where an already tight luxury market is feeling the impact.
  • It has been revealed that the AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation.
  • There are more than 2,000 AI companies operating in Upcoming York City, according to the city’s Economic Development Corporation, and AI companies signed leases for about 1.5 million square feet in just the first six months of 2026, the Brooklyn Daily Eagle reported.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The artificial intelligence boom has expanded from the rolling hills of San Francisco and Silicon Valley to the busy streets of New York City, where an already tight luxury market is feeling the impact.

It has been revealed that the AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation. With the tech constantly growing and producing newly minted millionaires, the impacts of deep-pocketed AI professionals entering the New York real estate market are just beginning to be felt, agents there say.

There are more than 2,000 AI companies operating in Upcoming York City, according to the city’s Economic Development Corporation, and AI companies signed leases for about 1.5 million square feet in just the first six months of 2026, the Brooklyn Daily Eagle reported.

Major AI frontrunners like Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, and EliseAI have opened offices in New York, contributing to the thriving commercial real estate market.

“It’s been pretty unbelievable, what’s happening in the public sphere of the AI business. We’re seeing a ton of AI leasing activity on the ground in Fresh York,” Evan Kleinberg, co-founder of Cornelia Street Partners, a boutique commercial real estate firm, told Realtor.com. “And it’s been happening so fast, it’s almost representative of the technology itself. The companies hire immediately and they need space yesterday.”.

In a recent development, while Kleinberg has been keeping eyes on the AI industry for the past couple of years, his brokerage worked with its first AI specific manufacturer about 12 months ago, at the end of 2025. Since then, the brokerage has secured leases for five companies developing proprietary AI models.

There are a number of reasons Kleinberg sees AI companies expanding east and planting roots in New York. The city has fully rebounded from the pandemic and has an attractive lifestyle that draws many young professionals. Plus, companies see the benefit of being close to their portfolio businesses.

“Ultimately, if your goal is to raise money from Goldman Sachs or JP Morgan or one of the major private equity groups like Apollo, they’re all here,” Kleinberg explained. “So wanting to get close to them is an underlying reason to move.”.

With these new offices comes a hoard of young, newly wealthy professionals who are looking to build a home in New York, many of whom are stepping into an already fiercely competitive luxury real estate market.

“Wall Street has historically been a major driver of Manhattan luxury real estate, and now we’re really starting to see the effects of AI. It’s becoming an important engine for wealth creation and housing demand,” Michelle Griffith, a residential real estate agent in Latest York City, told Realtor.com. “Right now in Manhattan, we are already in a very tight rental market. Even for the last year, rents are up anywhere from 10% to 20% in Manhattan, especially for these luxury properties.”.

As of November, the median sold price of a home in Manhattan is $1,150,000, a 15% year over year increase. Some Manhattan neighborhoods have had more extreme changes.

Industry observers note that the Lower East Side, for example, saw the median sale price jump 28% year over year to $1,435,000. Rent in the Lower East Side also increased 11% year over year, for a median of $5,947 per month.

The Newly introduced York City luxury residential landscape is no stranger to competition, with deep pocketed masses vying for a severely limited inventory of spaces. With the flood of AI professionals, another layer of people has been added to the market.

Griffith recalled a recent listing at 50 Gramercy Park North, which had historically rented for $30,000. While a rental like this, which is in the higher end of the market, would previously take 30 to 60 days to identify a tenant, the listing had eight rental bids after 48 hours on the market, with half above asking.

Most workers are determined to live close to work, making it especially challenging to secure an apartment in these highly sought after neighborhoods.

OpenAI’s 90,000-square-foot Newly introduced York office is located in the Puck Building, which sits on the boarder of SoHo and Nolita in Manhattan.

Anthropic’s Newly introduced York hub takes up the entirety of a 16-story building at 330 Hudson Street in the Hudson Square neighborhood of Lower Manhattan.

“The offices are in fantastic locations, so it’s easy to find great housing within walking distance,” noted Griffith. “The challenge is finding that apartment because there is very, very limited inventory because those neighborhoods were already popular and in demand.”.

For luxury agents, the challenge is no longer finding tenants with the money to rent high priced rentals, its finding the rentals for deep pocketed tenants.

Recent findings suggest that when Griffith began in real estate 15 years ago, an apartment for $100,000 per month might be the biggest rental of the year. Now, rentals for $80,000 to even $150,000 are common and moving promptly, she shared.

Power-efficient inference chips are becoming the entry price for enterprises that want to run AI on hardware they own.

As AI shifts from building models to running them every day, costly graphics processing unit racks and the liquid cooling they demand keep many companies renting compute instead. That gap is opening room for challengers to the incumbent chipmakers. Axelera AI B.V. built its business at the edge with low-power chips and edge AI development tools, and it is now taking that technology into data center infrastructure, according to Manuel Botija (pictured), vice president and head of product at Axelera.

“Enterprises cannot own their own infrastructure. They’re locked out because of the cost and the power,” Botija said. “We are enabling them now to own it. It’s not that we are helping the world save power or save money — which we are — but it’s that we are unlocking use cases that were simply not possible before.”.

It has been revealed that botija spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how power-efficient inference chips are heading for the data center and how enterprises locked out by the cost and power of GPU racks can own their own AI infrastructure instead of renting compute. (* Disclosure below.).

Industry observers note that “Having a six-kilowatt server that can perform like a data centre GPU is a pretty major deal,” he noted. “It basically means that they have some storage equipment, some networking equipment, some traditional CPU equipment, and next to all of that, they can also insert some AI inference hardware acceleration without needing to go and rebuild another server room or another data center.”.

According to recent reports, for enterprises that would rather own their AI hardware than pay a recurring cloud bill, the barriers have been steep. A GPU rack costs at least $1 million, often far more, and usually requires liquid cooling, Botija noted. Axelera’s answer rests on digital in-memory computing, a technique that grew out of its founders’ research and gives the manufacturer’s power-efficient inference chips a performance-per-watt advantage.

Recent findings suggest that “Now you can own your own infrastructure,” Botija remarked. “You can amortize those investments and … reduce your opex, and therefore be more profitable as a firm.”.

Could GTA 6 be stealing retail’s attention just as digital asset markets struggle to bring individual investors back?

The scale of the launch is hard to ignore. Reports put GTA 6 pre-orders at well over 10 million copies before its worldwide release. The game also carries expectations of $1.85 billion in revenue during its first three days.

Workers are making room for it, too. BambooHR data indicated time-off requests for launch day running 9% to 17% above a typical third Thursday of November. A separate Zety survey found 22% of Gen Z workers planned around the release.

That is a sizeable chunk of the demographic that crypto platforms have spent years trying to attract. Gaming and crypto compete for the same online attention, particularly among younger audiences who spend hours on streaming platforms, social media and digital communities.

For us, checking Bitcoin prices, chasing the latest meme coin and following market-moving posts can easily become part of the daily routine. But GTA 6 offers something considerably more entertaining than watching another sideways trading session.

The launch is also driving enormous engagement across YouTube and Reddit. Sensor Tower estimates point to more than 50 million additional visits to food delivery and restaurant apps in the US over 30 days.

Crypto’s social media ecosystem could find itself competing for a much smaller share of that attention.

It has been revealed that there is another reason the timing is interesting. Retail crypto trading has been weakening even as the broader market has attracted fresh capital.

In a recent development, eToro clients placed 62% fewer crypto trades in October than a year earlier. Robinhood’s crypto trading volume also fell 48% year over year in October, while Coinbase consumer spot volume dropped 59%.

The figures show that rising market valuations have not translated into the same level of retail trading activity seen during previous cycles.

Recent findings suggest that this leaves crypto exposed to competition for speculative attention. Institutional investors can continue trading through market cycles, but retail often depends on excitement, momentum, and whatever narrative is dominating the internet.

It has been revealed that but GTA 6 has all three. The game could temporarily pull casual traders away from exchanges, particularly those who spend their evenings chasing small-cap tokens and following crypto KOLs. Meme coins could be especially vulnerable if their usual audience spends the next several days exploring Vice City instead.

There is also an ironic possibility that GTA 6 could create fresh opportunities for crypto speculation. Gaming-themed tokens and GTA-related meme coins could attract traders looking to profit from the launch itself.

Sources indicate that bitcoin does not need gamers watching charts every minute to keep trading. But an industry built around speculation, online communities, and retail enthusiasm cannot afford to ignore where that attention goes.

What we learned from Nvidia’s first earnings call without Jensen Huang

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, nvidia Corp.
  • Revenue more than doubled year-over-year.
  • In a recent development, this was Nvidia’s first earnings call without co-founder Jensen Huang, whose resignation as president and chief executive was revealed on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 14:32 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

ANALYSIS by Zeus Kerravala.

According to recent reports, nvidia Corp. reported its quarterly results this week, and contrary to the prevailing narrative, the sky didn’t fall.

Revenue more than doubled year-over-year. The Vera Rubin chip platform achieved the fastest product ramp in the organization’s history, and management raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to roughly 75%, up from 70%. By all accounts, it was a solid beat and raise.

In a recent development, this was Nvidia’s first earnings call without co-founder Jensen Huang, whose resignation as president and chief executive was revealed on Nov. 12. Board Chair Harvey Jones told investors that the resignation followed the “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the tech giant’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” Hours after Huang publicly mentioned he would be willing to return, Jones said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and would not take questions about the circumstances or the board’s ongoing investigation.

In a recent development, colette Kress, the longtime chief financial officer who is now also serving as interim CEO, set the tone in her first minute: “Our ambition will not change. Our passion for innovation will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change.”.

After listening to the call, I believe Nvidia answered the short-term question and left the long-term one open. The company made a convincing case that it can execute without its founder. It has yet to show who decides where it goes next. Here are five things we learned and what they mean for those who buy, budget for or operate artificial intelligence infrastructure.

In a recent development, the fear going into the call was disruption. The quarter closed before Huang’s exit, so the results can’t settle that. The guidance can, and it went up. Hyperscalers brought Vera Rubin into production in about a month, half the time Grace Blackwell required. The roadmap is set through Vera Rubin Ultra next year and Feynman in 2028, and Kress remarked the supply agreements extend through the end of the decade.

She explained that the past month has been “Business as usual.” Kress added, “We’ve engaged with our customers, suppliers and partners. They’re all 100% behind us.” She also noted that TSMC leadership was at Nvidia’s offices this week.

I have long held that Nvidia’s moat was never the silicon. It’s the accumulated layers of systems, software and supply chain built around it. The past week was the first real test of that view, and so far, it’s holding. A yearly product cadence this complex runs on thousands of engineers and a supply chain planned years in advance.

Recent findings suggest that asked about talent retention, Kress acknowledged that “there are diverse opinions” among employees while insisting they are “committed to doing their life’s work” at Nvidia. The firm’s talent can’t be overstated, and although Huang was the face of the company, the employees are what made it tick.

Sources indicate that earlier this week, Cisco Systems Inc. CEO Chuck Robbins appeared with Brian Sozzi. When asked whether he still trusts Nvidia, Robbins replied immediately, “Absolutely.” He added, “The industry’s bigger than one person. I don’t care how good you are. There are a lot of smart people. There are 42,000 people at Nvidia. So I’m not all that concerned.” Huang may have been the most visible Nvidia employee, but the manufacturer is full of smart, driven people. Leadership understands this, and I expect turnover to have minimal impact.

Employee retention is a top-of-mind issue for Nvidia executives. Business Insider reported this week that the firm held its first all-hands meeting after Huang. The article noted that Kress declared intends to accelerate pay raises and equity grants, Jones discussed the CEO search and Buck outlined the roadmap. It’s reasonable to believe that Huang’s departure was a shock to employees, but the business goes on, and I expect things to settle down in short order.

For information technology buyers, nothing changes about what you’ve ordered or planned over the next 18 to 24 months. Don’t pause a deployment because of a leadership headline. The advice I gave in August still applies: Welcome Nvidia’s simplification and hedge the dependency.

One of the more interesting comments on the call came from Jones, not Kress. In describing the CEO search, which will consider both internal and external candidates, he mentioned the board “appreciates that we’re living in a world where advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are driving major changes in our marketplace. Our newly introduced CEO will need to navigate those waters carefully.”.

Sources indicate that that was paired with immediate action. On the morning of earnings, the board created a standing national security and export control oversight committee of three directors that will retain outside experts. Kress disclosed that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China and noted that the U.S. Commerce Department issued fresh export controls this week, which the manufacturer “still has some time to study.”.

Huang was a product visionary who also served as the industry’s chief diplomat. The board is now signaling that fluency in Washington is a core requirement, on par with technical vision.

Industry observers note that for IT leaders at multinationals, export policy is now a deployment variable. The upcoming Commerce rule is intended to block remote access to advanced chips via data centers in third countries, so the location of your capacity and who can access it are now compliance questions. Bring your compliance team into AI infrastructure planning early.

Sources indicate that with demand still far ahead of supply, who gets Nvidia systems matters more than what they cost. Kress laid out the criteria more clearly than I’ve heard before. First are land, power and shell, meaning whether a customer’s facility is ready to receive and use the gear in the quarter it ships. Second is capital. Third, for customers that aren’t investment-grade, is proof of off-take, or evidence that someone has committed to use the capacity.

In a recent development, “All are getting the same pricing,” Kress stated. “That is super notable for us, and we just need to assure that they are ready on their side in terms of being able to accept the compute.”.

Sources indicate that those same factors were incorporated into the guidance. Kress stated the outlook “considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.” The reality is that the AI bottleneck has shifted from the chip to the building, the grid and the balance sheet. Nvidia is serving as the industry’s underwriter, determining who is ready.

The lesson for enterprise buyers is that readiness is the currency. If you want on-premises systems, secure power, cooling and funding before requesting allocation. If you can’t, buy capacity from a provider that has already cleared this hurdle. In my view, this also helps explain why sovereign AI is growing so promptly for Nvidia. Those projects often arrive with land and power already in place.

It has been revealed that over the past year, Nvidia has used its balance sheet to seed the ecosystem through guarantees, investments, and commitments to neoclouds and AI labs. Though  neoclouds remain important, Kress brought a different tone to this audience. She mentioned Nvidia will “continue to be disciplined and selective” in supporting neoclouds and that it is “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees” as other sources of capital become available. Asked about vendor financing, she acknowledged that “a lot of things have changed over this last quarter.”.

Two notable details emerged during the call. When Bernstein Research analyst Stacy Rasgon pressed on what he read as new disclosure language about neocloud commitments, Kress explained that Nvidia’s guarantees take effect only after a partner has raised its own debt and equity, built the facility and installed the compute. If the project stalls, the guarantee lapses.

“Is it new? No. Did we change anything? No,” she said. Even so, spelling it out clarifies Nvidia’s participation in neoclouds. When asked about uses of capital beyond the share buyback, which she said Nvidia still plans to complete, she put suppliers first: “The top priority is going to be our suppliers.” Prepayments to expand capacity come before customer financing, which will be reserved for “very strong customers.”.

This was a critical piece of information for investors. I’ve previously compared vendor-financed neoclouds to the CLECs of the internet era, where the financing organization was left holding the bag. A CFO-led Nvidia appears to see the same risk. The result is a shakeout in which well-capitalized neoclouds with contracted demand grow stronger, while thinly funded ones struggle to secure systems. This should offer some comfort to investors that circular financing has been de-risked.

Sources indicate that the flip side is that someone still must fund the buildout outside the hyperscalers. Kress pointed to infrastructure capital partners establishing financing platforms. Whether that money arrives as fast as Nvidia steps back is what to watch for.

My advice to IT buyers is to ask, before signing a multiyear deal with a neocloud, how it’s financed, how much capacity is committed and where it stands in Nvidia’s allocation queue. Those were niche questions a year ago. They should be standard due diligence now.

Industry observers note that the demand story has shifted from training models to running agents, broadening what customers need from Nvidia. Citing OpenRouter data, Kress said agentic workloads now account for roughly 80% of tokens. Falling token prices are driving more usage, keeping GPU rental rates climbing.

The CPU growth story shouldn’t surprise anyone. In May, I wrote that agentic AI opens a massive newly introduced spigot for Nvidia on the CPU side. This quarter, demand outpaced supply. “Agentic AI is driving extraordinary demand for CPUs, far outstripping supply,” Kress said, noting that Nvidia’s Vera CPU is now adopted by CoreWeave, Meta, Nscale and Open AI. Agents spend much of their time calling tools, running code and moving data, which is general-purpose work. A CPU shortage amid a GPU boom highlights how quickly the workload is changing.

Nvidia is also filling in the layers above and around the hardware. The agent safety platform pairs OpenShell, which limits what agents can access, with Sentry, which runs on BlueField data processing units and monitors agent behavior in silicon. In my view, the biggest barrier to deploying agents in production is control, not model quality.

The network is part of this, too. Kress mentioned co-packaged optics is in volume production, and Lambda’s deployment, declared at this week’s SC26 conference, is the first large-scale proof point. Nvidia is a formidable networking vendor, though buyers mixing accelerators will still want to weigh a network supplier that isn’t also selling a competing chip.

For IT buyers, proposal CPU capacity for agent workloads now, and insist that agent controls reside outside the model, in infrastructure you can audit.

It has been revealed that the question of who the upcoming CEO will be might not be just about Nvidia but about the entire industry. If the board goes internal, Ian Buck seems to be the frontrunner. Externally, the names most bandied about are Advanced Micro Devices Inc. CEO Lisa Su, Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas and Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian, or we could see Manuvir Das make a comeback and return to the tech giant.

It has been revealed that most industry watchers describe Nvidia as a chip manufacturer, a view that is about a decade out of date. Nvidia’s value comes from the full systems it has built around its silicon. Each is a stack tailored to an industry: hardware, libraries, frameworks, pretrained models, simulation and developer tools, all tuned to work together.

According to recent reports, the next CEO must treat silicon as a key layer of an open, secure, agentic enterprise stack. Enterprises won’t buy GPUs. They’ll buy outcomes: agents that run safely on governed data across clouds, on-premises and at the edge. Whoever runs Nvidia next must sell that outcome, play well within an ecosystem Nvidia doesn’t fully control, and make security a core part of the platform. Here are three dark-horse candidates to consider:.

Matt Garman. The Amazon Web Services Inc. CEO has led the world’s largest cloud through the shift to AI. He knows what it takes to turn infrastructure into consumable services at enormous scale. Garman also lives the open-stack approach: AWS offers model choice, runs its own Trainium chips alongside Nvidia’s, and sells to enterprises that want flexibility rather than lock-in. He would bring operational discipline and a deep feel for the customer. The question is whether Nvidia’s biggest customer-turned-competitor can credibly lead the supplier.

Jeetu Patel, Cisco Systems Inc.’s president and chief product officer, is the best storyteller in enterprise tech after Huang himself. He has spent the past few years rebuilding Cisco’s portfolio around secure AI infrastructure, integrating networking, security and observability into a single platform. That is exactly the “open, secure, agentic” stack Nvidia must deliver. Patel thinks in platforms, moves rapidly,and has been personally using AI agents to shape his product views. He also has deep enterprise credibility, which Nvidia needs more than additional credibility with hyperscalers.

Charlie Giancarlo, CEO of Everpure (formerly Pure Storage), may be the most underrated name here. He built networking businesses at Cisco, spent time in private equity, and has repositioned Pure as a data management tech giant. Storage revenue is growing thanks to hyperscaler wins. Giancarlo understands that agentic AI depends on data and that the data layer and the network are where enterprise AI succeeds or fails. He is a systems thinker who has led a platform transition before.

In a recent development, two final points on the CEO hire: For some reason, there is a tremendous amount of industry chatter that Jensen Huang was the only person at Nvidia with key relationships with suppliers, partners, and other ecosystem providers. I know for a fact that is not true. Nvidia’s leadership, which includes Buck, Deb Shoquist (executive vice president of operations), Nico Caprez (vice president of global AI development), Gilad Shainer and Kevin Deierling (networking leadership), Kress and others, all have deep relationships with the ecosystem.

Industry observers note that also, I wouldn’t expect the board to make a snap decision about its next CEO. The roadmap is baked beyond Feynman, and the company can continue for a couple of years, if needed. This is an crucial hire; the board should take its time and ensure it’s the right person.

This call confirmed what many industry watchers, including me, have long believed: The moat was built in layers, and those layers held. Supply is constrained, the roadmap is set and customers are still asking for more than Nvidia can build.

Kress closed the call by saying, “We’ve got this.” On execution, I believe her. Kress is a steady hand right now, and the discipline she brings to capital allocation should make the AI buildout healthier. The bets that created Nvidia’s position, though, were placed years before the market arrived. Post-Jensen, Nvidia will continue to perform as it did; as Robbins put it, no one is bigger than the industry.

My advice to IT buyers is to stick with current plans and closely monitor the CEO search. Since Nvidia’s roadmap is baked through Feynman and beyond, it can ride momentum for the next two years or longer.

Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engel & Völkers declared an Aruba shop, Realty of America entered San Diego, and eXp Realty added a Tampa Bay brokerage and an Ohio team.

It has been revealed that brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into new markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies. Engel & Völkers is headed to Aruba, where it plans to open a shop in April 2027, and Realty of America reached California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 of her Team Z Realty agents in San Diego.

eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX. Baird & Warner brought on Oak Park, Illinois, boutique Beyond Properties, and Dane Briggs teamed up with Phil Sexton at HomeSmart’s NEXT team. IRES MLS welcomed back a former staffer to run operations, and Howard Hanna Portside added an agent in Massachusetts.

Engel & Völkers expanded into Aruba with license partners Zobaida Akkari and Richard Franken, Aruba-based entrepreneurs with backgrounds in real estate, luxury sales, hospitality and tourism. The shop is projected to open in April 2027 at L.G. Smith Blvd. 330 in Palm Beach and will serve clients across the island, according to the company.

“Aruba is a compelling addition to the network’s growing presence in the Caribbean,” Stuart Siegel, president and CEO of Engel & Völkers Americas, said in a statement.

It has been revealed that realty of America entered California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 Team Z Realty agent partners in San Diego. Ulloa has generated more than $4.2 billion in sales volume over her 13-year career, and Team Z peaked at 72 agents and $589 million in annual volume, according to the company. Agent-owned ROA, founded in September 2024, notes it has more than 3,900 agents across 26 markets.

“People around me may see what I am giving up, but I see what I am making room for,” Ulloa said in a statement.

It has been revealed that rene Carpena and Dana Carpena moved Florida’s 1st Choice Realty, their independent Greater Tampa Bay brokerage, to eXp Realty, where it now operates as 1st Choice Collective. The group brings more than 70 agents and support staff and recorded more than 325 transactions and $60 million in sales volume in 2025, according to the tech giant.

Industry observers note that jon Bowling also brought his 17-person team in Mason, Ohio, to eXp after 20 years with RE/MAX. eXp Realty is the core subsidiary of AGNT Inc.

Baird & Warner added Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage in Oak Park, Illinois, whose dozen agents will operate as Beyond Properties Group. Owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, who founded the firm almost 20 years ago, will co-lead the group with team leader Cynthia Howe Gajewski. The group joins Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office and keeps its Marion Street location.

“This partnership will allow me to simplify the operational side of the business and spend more time doing what I love, which is focusing on our agents and clients,” Cuneen said in a statement.

It has been revealed that dane Briggs, an Arizona real estate veteran, partnered with Phil Sexton, founder of HomeSmart’s NEXT team, in a leadership role focused on agent workflows and AI integrations. Briggs has worked as a designated broker and title executive, founded referral brokerage Roosted and led expansion initiatives at Homie. He has also served as an Inman Ambassador.

In a recent development, “Before long, we weren’t just talking about what Phil was building. We were talking about what we could build together,” Briggs said in a statement.

IRES MLS, which serves Northern Colorado and parts of the Front Range, rehired Samantha Ewing as director of operations. Ewing spent 13 years at IRES as a projects manager and quality assurance tester before leaving in 2018, and she has more than 20 years of experience in MLS operations and real estate technology.

“Having Samantha return to IRES is an exciting opportunity for our team and the local industry we serve,” CEO Julie Dahl said in a statement.

In a recent development, howard Hanna Portside Real Estate Group added Melissa Winter, an agent with nearly 15 years of experience who focuses on first-time homebuyers, to its Massachusetts team in Amesbury. Portside, which has more than 200 agents, entered a strategic partnership with Howard Hanna in 2026, according to the company.

“What drew me to Portside was the energy, the people, and the opportunity for growth,” Winter said in a statement.

How an Artsy Pennsylvania River Town Became an Architectural Powerhouse Where Old Meets New

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1284 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At first glance, Latest Hope, PA, looks like little more than a picturesque, upscale river town with a vibrant arts scene.
  • Located halfway between Latest York City and Philadelphia, New Hope spans roughly 1.42 square miles and is home to fewer than 3,000 year-round residents.
  • In Fresh Hope's luxury housing market, old and new blend seamlessly: 18th-century structures are brought into the 21st century with bold, modern additions and amenities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At first glance, Latest Hope, PA, looks like little more than a picturesque, upscale river town with a vibrant arts scene. However, a closer look reveals that the historic borough shares an architectural DNA with Europe's premier capitals.

Located halfway between Latest York City and Philadelphia, New Hope spans roughly 1.42 square miles and is home to fewer than 3,000 year-round residents. Yet it boasts an outsized reputation as a beloved regional tourist destination renowned for its art galleries, boutiques, riverside dining, and cultural institutions, led by the iconic Bucks County Playhouse, which has hosted major stars such as Grace Kelly, Robert Redford, and Liza Minnelli.

In Fresh Hope's luxury housing market, old and new blend seamlessly: 18th-century structures are brought into the 21st century with bold, modern additions and amenities.

"A lot of the homes around here, especially some of the larger homes, all started off as an old stone farmhouse, so incorporating some of that character while building the big steel and glass additions is very much an architectural vibe that is done here," Nicholas Esser, managing partner at Addison Wolfe Real Estate, tells Realtor.com®.

The market's remarkably varied housing stock also includes stately Colonial and Victorian homes, sprawling legacy estates, and cutting-edge newly introduced construction that would not look out of place in the heart of Silicon Valley.

In a recent development, architect Ralph Fey, with Ralph C. Fey Architects in Doylestown, PA, explains that New Hope's signature look is rooted in regulatory necessity, because more than half of the town falls in a strictly regulated historic district, which rarely allows older buildings to be torn down to make way for new builds.

Rather than viewing zoning laws as a creative roadblock, Fey has made his professional mark by seamlessly merging history with contemporary living.

In a recent development, "Some of the best architecture is born out of constraints," he tells Realtor.com. "The goal, the fun, the challenge is how to maintain that historic feel, meet the guidelines of the historic district, but provide the amenities that we now want to have as we live on the water.".

According to recent reports, maureen Reynolds, a Serhant luxury real estate agent in Newly introduced Hope, counts herself among Fey's clients. She at the moment lives in an 1832-built converted horse barn with tall ceilings and hand-hewn beams.

"I have all the modern amenities because of Ralph," she tells Realtor.com.

While Upcoming Hope lacks the urban density and wealth of major metros, Fey notes, its architectural style "is more like London, where you have newer construction next to historic construction, next to really historic construction, and it is that fabric that makes London so exciting.".

Founded in the 18th century on the banks of the Delaware River, New Hope was previously called Wells Ferry and later Coryell’s Ferry.

Recent findings suggest that the borough was rechristened after a fire in 1790 destroyed several mills owned by local businessman Benjamin Parry. He rebuilt them as the Upcoming Hope Mills, inspiring the town’s optimistic new name.

By the late 19th century, Fresh Hope had gained a reputation as an art colony and emerged as a major hub for American and Pennsylvania Impressionists, including William Langson Lathrop, Edward Willis Redfield, and Daniel Garber.

"New Hope definitely has an architectural richness that's been developed over centuries," states Reynolds. "Its historic buildings' relationship to the river and surrounding landscape give it a character that cannot be created overnight. And the challenge and opportunity for the architects, for Realtors®, and for developers is to respect that history while designing homes that accommodate the way people live today.".

Fey agrees, maintaining that Upcoming Hope's success as a thriving housing market is rooted in its past and the borough's fierce commitment to protecting it.

According to recent reports, "The same little river town 5 miles down the road that did not have a historic district, where all the homes were knocked down, would not have that feel of a classic historic town, and would not have that charm, and it could potentially lose it," he says. "It's really key to us as architects to preserve that feeling, and that's part of the reason why Upcoming Hope is as prized and treasured as it is—it's for its history.".

Even with new construction, a premium is placed on designing in harmony with the town.

In a recent development, fey and Reynolds frequently work with clients to select natural building materials such as locally sourced stone, cedar wood, and slate roof tiles. They complement surrounding centuries-old structures rather than clashing with the local aesthetic.

Sources indicate that "Most of my clients are very in love with the feel of the historic Newly introduced Hope and also would like to see some of the amenities of slightly more glass, slightly higher ceilings," says the architect. "So when we are doing additions on the traditional homes or existing historic housing stock, our goal is to contribute to the street.".

According to recent reports, despite its modest size, Upcoming Hope commands an impressively broad appeal. Esser and Fey say buyers range from locals looking to upgrade or build their dream homes to affluent transplants from neighboring New York, Philadelphia, and New Jersey hunting for a primary residence or weekend pied-à-terre, alongside retirees drawn to Pennsylvania's favorable tax climate.

Some home shoppers, however, come from much farther afield.

Reynolds’ roster of Newly introduced Hope clients includes buyers from the South of France, Sweden, Canada, and Japan, cementing the town’s status as a market punching well above its weight.

In August, the Philadelphia Business Journal ranked New Hope as the nation's No. 2 hottest luxury housing market during the second quarter of 2026 among 327 markets analyzed.

"That's an extraordinary distinction for a community of this size," notes Reynolds.

Prices have surged accordingly. Reynolds recounts how townhomes originally priced between $1.4 million and $1.8 million jumped to $2 million–$3.2 million in less than three years.

The latest Realtor.com housing data highlights that in October, the median listing price in Latest Hope topped $2 million, up more than 27% from a year ago.

Meanwhile, the luxury-tier threshold—representing the top 10% of the market—was just over $5 million.

While inventory was up more than 50% year over year last month, Realtor.com senior economist Hannah Jones notes that supply still remains nearly 60% below pre-pandemic levels.

“Demand comes largely from cash-rich buyers in the surrounding region, including a growing share from Newly introduced Jersey alongside the New York metro, who are insulated from mortgage rates hovering around 7%,” she notes.

As always with real estate, location remains paramount.

"If I have something on the river, it usually sells within a couple days, and that can be something, too, that is not turnkey—we're talking about something that can be slightly a shell inside," notes Reynolds.

Ultimately, what keeps buyers flocking to New Hope from near and far is the sheer architectural variety packed into the pint-sized, picture-perfect historic borough.

"The beautiful thing around here is that there's gorgeous properties everywhere, and the home styles do change between the more modern construction, with the beams and 12-foot ceilings, and old stone construction, but they mesh really well," concludes Esser.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jumping out of a helicopter into water below, rappelling down a 22-story building, enduring chemical warfare gas exposure — if you’ve never seen Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test, these are just a few of the tasks that must be completed.

It’s a reality TV show in which celebrities do physical challenges from the actual Special Forces selection process playbook. It’s like a competition show, but there are no eliminations, and no one gets voted off.

According to recent reports, to leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order. During the final test, the DS ejects those who fail the interrogation or selection test.

It has been revealed that season 5 is set in the Malaysian jungle. It features Candace Cameron Bure, Brandi Glanville, Oliver Hudson, Ruby Rose, George Santos, Bre Tiesi, Matt Barnes, and Mauricio and Alexia Umansky, among others.

It has been revealed that at the time that this article was published, Alexia was still in the competition. Mauricio voluntarily withdrew after a rib injury sustained during a hand-to-hand fighting challenge with former NBA player Matt Barnes. Mauricio said the injury took two or three months to heal.

The following challenge involved gas, and Mauricio didn’t think his ribs could take it. He mentioned he feared having a bad lung injury in the Malaysian jungle. Alexia agreed with the decision, saying the gas was the “most painful thing” she’d ever experienced in her life.

Inman spoke to Mauricio and Alexia midway through the season about the experience, the latest industry news and what’s next for The Agency.

What follows is the conversation, edited for length and clarity.

I believe sellers should have choice, but I believe that we should be sharing those private listings amongst everybody — every agent, every brokerage firm, not just keeping it for themselves. I feel like there’s a lot happening right now in the industry where everybody’s really looking out for themselves: the MLSs, NAR, Compass.

Actually, Compass, I think, wants to collaborate, wants to share, but they’re in a substantial, big fight. But in the meantime, this Clear Cooperation Policy is what is allowing them to keep all the listings to themselves and not share them … The PLS is exactly what that was, and I still think that if Clear Cooperation Policy didn’t pass, it would have been an amazing business to have right now.

Mauricio: We are really positioned as the premier luxury brokerage firm outside of Compass right now. They’ve got Sotheby’s, they’ve got Christie’s, they’ve got all of those different brands, and we’re the only independent luxury brokerage firm out there right now.

So I’m excited to be in that position. Competitors make you better every single day … I’m excited in terms of where we sit, where we stand in a very difficult time; I’m not excited about the market. We really need to do some things to improve it. We’ve had three years of very, very difficult conditions, and it’s going to be very difficult for people to survive. And those that do survive will come out better.

I think we’re in a good position to survive, but we’ve got our work cut out for us over the next year, year and a half. But we’ll continue to grow. We’ll continue to expand, and I’m excited to just be a part of this industry. But man, it’s hard out there right now.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

California-born sculptor Chester Beach worked out of a New York City studio between 1907 and 1952, nabbing high-profile commissions from the Panama-Pacific International Exposition, as well as the 1928 Summer Olympics.

But, like many artists, he carved out space for a pastoral retreat away from the hustle and bustle.

In 1917, after living in Rome for a brief period, he and his wife, Eleanor Beach, established a home in Brewster, NY, in Putnam County, just 55 miles north of the city. They named the Arts & Crafts-style estate OldWalls.

Now these 10.49 acres—including four buildings, comprising a compound—is looking for a upcoming steward.

"There have only been three owners including the original family that owned it up until 2009," says listing agent Will Stuart, of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices Newly introduced England Properties. "My sellers have been there for two years.".

Listing for $4,150,000, the new owner won't be the first to seek a deeper connection to nature while still being close to Manhattan.

Stuart notes that this eight-bedroom, 6.5-bath spread is exceptionally tied to its origins.

"Each owner has become a steward of the property and has preserved extensive family photographs, memoirs and documents, and have really kept the story going, which is rare with these kinds of properties," he notes. "A lot of times the information gets lost along the way. The story has been preserved so well.".

It has been revealed that the estate includes a four-bedroom stone residence with plaster walls, hand-crafted stonework and stained glass. There’s also a separate guest studio with a kitchen, bath, sleeping loft and stone fireplace. And, a two-bedroom guest cottage dating back to the 1940s with cozy amenities such as a fireplace and screened-in porch.

Another way the property has been preserved is through art the original owners brought into the house.

It has been revealed that tiles collected from Spain, Guatemala and Italy are laid into the floor, says Stuart. He adds that "there’s actually a cluster of Roman floor tiles under the dining-room table.".

In a recent development, the kitchen’s chandelier was born out of a turntable Beach used for sculpting. Eleanor’s bird paintings (112 in all) are incorporated into the living room’s ceiling.

In a recent development, “There’s three outbuildings in addition to the main residence that all offer incredible living space and charm,” claims Stuart. “Each one of them has a story and a history.”.

For example, in the detached studio, which was built before the home, are many of Beach’s tools and hardware, as well as the original doors.

A buyer drawn to that history is who Stuart is courting. But it could also be an equestrian, as the property features a five-stall barn with a spacious one-bedroom apartment. Nearby are run-outs, rolling grass turnout paddocks, a riding field with access to trails, and a riding arena in the sand.

“We have a lot of equestrians that have moved into the community,” says Stuart. “A lot of the equestrian people travel to Florida in the winter so they’re here half the year, but most people are here year-round.” Two miles down the road is Old Salem Farm, a 120-acre boarding and training facility.

Above all, the buyer will likely be someone who likes to be near Manhattan but also have a countryside retreat, just like Beach once did.

In a recent development, this mirrors a trend Stuart continues to see among buyers. “People looking for more space, more privacy, but want to stay within close proximity to the city,” he indicates. “This is a real compound here. It’s someone who is hosting family or guests.”.
