📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz mentioned that the odds of Bitcoin hitting $90,000 by the end of 2026 are slim in light of prevailing macroeconomic headwinds and the growing likelihood that the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates.

During a live event with Anthony Scaramucci at the Digital Assets Forum in Newly introduced York City, Novogratz was asked if Bitcoin could get back to $90,000 by the end of this year.

"Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," Novogratz mentioned.

According to recent reports, his gloomy outlook comes as Bitcoin has struggled to rebound after a devastating drop that saw its price dip as low as $62,000 over the weekend. Bitcoin's price stood at around $64,600 on Nov. 17. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization has declined for six consecutive weeks.

A shift in the U.S. monetary policy outlook, namely the prospect of more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, has been largely to blame for Bitcoin's decline, according to Novogratz.

"At the start of the year, everybody thought the Fed was going to be cutting now," he noted.

But high inflation and ongoing supply shocks have forced investors to readjust their expectations.

According to recent reports, "Inflation's going up. We've got inflation going up," Novogratz noted, warning that inflationary pressures could become increasingly entrenched.

According to recent reports, "The Fed's going to hike. At least two more, probably three more," he remarked.

Novogratz predicted that the Fed would raise rates by 25 basis points in December and then hike again at its next meeting.

According to recent reports, he said that higher rates, at least in the near term, tend to weigh on Bitcoin. But the higher cost of government borrowing could eventually provide support for the cryptocurrency.

"Yeah, later," he stated in response to the suggestion that higher borrowing costs could be a tailwind for Bitcoin.

Industry observers note that "First, you're gonna hike rates. Oh, sell gold, right? You're going to go to the dollar. It's so ingrained in peoples' heads," he remarked.

"Carry costs going up," he said. Bitcoin doesn't offer the same yield as interest-bearing dollar assets.

"You don't make any interest on Bitcoin in dollars," he noted.

In particular, Novogratz mentioned that the massive rise in Treasury yields has been particularly detrimental to the crypto market.

Recent findings suggest that "Literally 40 basis points in like four days of trading. So that's why crypto's down," he said.

He also stated that the massive crypto hack could still be weighing on investors' minds, adding to market jitters.

"I think in the back of their minds is the hack," he stated.

Latest Update: Google adds computer use capabilities to Gemini’s Mac app

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google LLC today released a new version of Gemini’s Mac client that can interact with other apps on the user’s computer.
  • The feature is available in the U.S.
  • In a recent development, users can instruct Gemini to launch a local app by including the command “@Computer use” in their prompts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:41 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Google LLC today released a new version of Gemini’s Mac client that can interact with other apps on the user’s computer.

The feature is available in the U.S. on launch. It requires a Google AI subscription, which equips consumer Google accounts with a broader lineup of artificial intelligence tools. The offering also includes additional storage space and certain other features.

In a recent development, users can instruct Gemini to launch a local app by including the command “@Computer use” in their prompts. For example, a designer could upload a sketch of a vehicle and ask the AI assistant to turn it into a three-dimensional animation. Gemini finds the local app that is needed for the task, creates a project proposal and carries out the work step by step.

The assistant supports tasks that comprise dozens of actions. Furthermore, consumers can use the output of a newly completed Gemini workflow to launch follow-up projects. A user could have the assistant generate a visual asset in a design tool and then turn it into a mini-app with Visual Studio Code.

According to recent reports, gemini can interact with not only local apps but also web services. That means it can load data from webpages into programs that run on the user’s machine, as well as move data in the opposite direction and between cloud services.

In a recent development, the AI carries out its work in a background window. As a result, people don’t have to pause their work while the assistant is running. They can track Gemini workflows via a preview pane built into the Mac client’s chat window. Additionally, Google has included controls that make it possible to give Gemini feedback mid-task.

“Privacy and safety are built in: you choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause at any time, and approve key actions before they happen,” Michael Friedman, Google’s group product manager for the Gemini app, wrote in a blog post.

It has been revealed that the Mac version of Muse, Meta Platforms Inc.’s recently launched AI agent, can also interact with local apps and data. Furthermore, a cloud-based virtual machine enables it to perform tasks even when the user’s computer is offline. Dots, a competing service from OpenAI Group PBC, offers a similar capability.

Google may seek to match its rivals’ cloud-based workflow hosting features in the future. The tech giant can also extend Gemini in other ways. Notably, it could bring Gemini’s computer use mode to additional operating systems and add features for business users. OpenAI’s Dots already includes capabilities designed to automate business workflows such as procurement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A five-bedroom modern retreat nestled on a tree-lined street in Santa Monica, CA has just hit the market for $6,898,000.

Built in 1949, the 4,746-square-foot residence was renovated in 2022 and now features a sun-soaked open floor plan with curated finishes, designer lighting, and walls of windows.

It has been revealed that “I love all of the light that comes into the home,” said listing agent Shelton Wilder of Christie’s International Real Estate Southern California. “It has beautiful skylights throughout and it’s located on the side of the street that gets so much natural sunlight. It looks like a movie set.”.

Designed for grand-scale entertaining and everyday living, the thoughtful layout offers a lavish primary sanctuary separate from a second-story guest wing that could also be used for extended family.

Recent findings suggest that “The primary suite is so private and very luxurious,” Wilder noted. “It was the primary residence for the sellers, who have owned it for five years. I think the next buyer will use it as a primary as well. It was so special for the sellers who have three kids. It could also be someone with older kids who want to stay there while visiting.”.

A sleek chef’s kitchen has two refrigerators, double ovens, custom cabinetry, a breakfast bar, and a built-in coffee machine. Glass doors from the dining area open to the private backyard with an outdoor shower and a brand-newly introduced heated pool and spa.

Architectural details include a sunken sitting room with built-in seating, a living room with a fireplace, and a primary suite with access to two offices, one of which opens to a rooftop deck designed for soaking in the sweeping canyon views.

Industry observers note that “Santa Monica Canyon is a magical place to live,” she noted. “You can walk to the beach; Montana Avenue is very close for shopping and restaurants; and Canyon Elementary School is just a few minutes away as well.”.

A bonus playroom could double as a family room, and a commercial-grade fitness center occupies the lower level.

“It’s very rare for a house like this with this amount of square footage, two offices, a pool, and a gym to come up in this area,” Wilder added.
